newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU's Fischler sees need for further farm reform.
newsitem.headline: EU's Fischler sees need for further farm reform.

text.p: Reform of EU farm policy must continue to prevent crises in various market segments and to embrace new member states in eastern Europe, Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said.
"We shouldn't be too hasty but we shouldn't maintain the status quo either," he told a news conference during Germany's annual "Green Week" Farm Fair.

The EU in 1999 at the latest had to draw up new financial and structural plans in preparation for the new round of world trade talks and it needed to communicate to aspiring EU members details of the agricultural systems they would be joining.
"Only if we continue on this (reform) course, can we make demands on others," he said, alluding to U.S. and EU negotiations on competition in world food markets.

While the EU had successfully cut farm spending and output volumes, the crisis over mad cow disease and its possible human links had shown how fragile the EU farm system was and how quickly new costs and surpluses could arise, Fischler said.
He called the mad cow issue the "greatest crisis ever in the EU."

Negotiations with 10 applicants to join the EU would start in 1998 at the earliest, Fischler said. It was unlikely that they would join at the same date but there would be long transition periods, bridged by free trade agreements.
The eastern Europeans needed to restructure their inefficient farming systems and the EU would support this process with special transition funds.
Spain also needed 12 years until full accession, he noted.

Fischler also said the EU must provide for when a "peace clause" allowing certain production-related farm payments ended in 2002. The EU must decouple these payments from output, for example by linking them to rural ecological services, to avoid massive pressure from competitors.
